Define a vector control intervention in an OpenMalaria scenario

Source: R/xml_export.R
define_OM_vector_control.Rd

Writes the definition of a vector control intervention (ITN or IRS) into an openMalariaUtilities baseList, for both model structures: the components of the generic vector intervention (GVI) of add_OM_GVI (deterrency, pre-prandial killing in the standard model, post-prandial killing). Deploy it with deploy_OM_vector_control and the same name.

For dummy-host interventions, the host-seeking killing is written by deploy_OM_vector_control(), one dummy host per campaign; define_OM_vector_control() keeps what it needs in baseList$anophelesmodel (not written to the XML) and says so in a message.

What has been checked in OpenMalaria. Run through openMalariaUtilities and checked on the entomological outputs:

  • OpenMalaria 44: standard ITNs deployed by campaigns: each effect (deterrency, pre- and post-prandial killing) changes its own parameter, in the in-bed mosquito populations only; Weibull decays (exact and fitted); refresh on redeployment; baseline EIR and population contributions.

  • OpenMalaria 49: standard ITNs (the same effects as in 44); dummy-host nets (below: timing, coverage, replacement by later campaigns, populations reached and lifespan as designed; the decay of the added hosts follows the written decay within 0.3% of the initial effect); a named list of nets with placeholder decays (identical to the nets defined separately); IRS, with both irs_exposure definitions of get_OM_ento_snippet; deployments restricted by age and with cumulative coverage; continuous deployment (om_continuous).

The plain-text route (get_OM_xml) writes the same XML as the openMalariaUtilities route (package tests, and for schema 49). Not run in OpenMalaria: deployments restricted to a sub-population (subpop).

Host-seeking killing (OpenMalaria schema >= 46). OpenMalaria's GVI has no host-seeking killing. In this package it is a dummy host per covered person, of availability KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute \(\times\) insecticide decay (relative to the human availability \(\alpha_h\)), on which every mosquito that finds it dies. It is written as OpenMalaria non-human hosts: for each campaign \(k\) (date \(t_k\), coverage \(c_k\)), an added non-human host <name>_dummy_<k> (addNonHumanHosts, deployed at \(t_k\)), of availability relative to an adult human \(c_k \times\) KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute \(/ \alpha_h\) (\(\alpha_h\) of the population's model) and biting probability 0, whose availability decays as the GVI effects do: attrition \(\times\) insecticide decay of host-seeking killing, exact when it is a single OpenMalaria decay, otherwise the Weibull fitted to their product (one nonHumanHostsModifications <name>_dummy_<k>_decay, omitted for a constant decay: an availability reduction of 1 with an increasing decay multiplies the availability by the decay). As for the GVI, whose components are refreshed (not stacked) in people who receive them again, a campaign replaces the nets of its recipients: each earlier dummy host is reduced by the coverage \(c_k\) of every later campaign \(k\) (<name>_dummy_<j>_replaced_<k>, constant availability reduction \(c_k\), the same number or placeholder as the schedule), which gives the expected effect of campaigns reaching random, independent shares of the population. Increasing decays need OpenMalaria schema 46 or later (checked with 49): the OMVersion of the baseList. As for the GVI effects, a rising insecticide decay (negative halflife_insecticide) is only exported through the fitted Weibull (with attrition). Host-seeking killing acts on the same populations as the GVI (in bed for ITNs).

Reference human. OpenMalaria multiplies the relative availability of an added host by the availability of an average adult, the person sleeping in the experimental hut where host-seeking killing was measured. Relative to the average human of the population, which is the human of this package's model, the host-seeking killing is therefore stronger in OpenMalaria than in this package, by the ratio of adult to mean human availability (1.35 in the scenario checked, Tanzanian demography; it depends on the age structure). This choice may be revisited.

Placeholders, only where something varies.

  • Efficacies: written for one intervention; placeholders ("@<name>_deterrency@", "@<name>_preprandial@", "@<name>_postprandial@") for a named list of several interventions (e.g. nets or parameterisations to choose between in scenarios). A list defines one intervention, deployed under name; each scenario uses the values of one of its interventions.

  • Decays: with decay = "fixed" (default), written from the interventions (which must then have the same decays); with decay = "placeholder", "@<name>_deterrency_L@" (and _k when the decay function has a shape parameter), ... Each effect keeps its decay function when it is the same for all the interventions (e.g. a step for historical nets), and is otherwise a Weibull (exact, or fitted).

  • Dummy hosts: availabilities written when one intervention and numeric coverages fix them; otherwise "@<name>_dummy_<k>_pop<j>@" (campaign \(k\), mosquito population \(j\): row of om_ento$shares, printed by the message). Their decay follows decay as an effect of its own: with "placeholder", "@<name>_hsk_L@" (and _k).

All interventions of a list must use the same model structure. Fill the placeholders of a scenario table with om_scenario_values.

Requires the openMalariaUtilities package (see add_OM_GVI).

Usage

define_OM_vector_control(
  baseList,
  interv,
  intervention_type = c("ITN", "IRS"),
  name = NULL,
  decay = c("fixed", "placeholder")
)

Arguments

baseList

openMalariaUtilities baseList, with the entomology written by define_OM_entomology (whose mosquito populations and parameters are used).

interv

Intervention from om_vector_control (or an object from build_intervention), or a named list of them (template).

intervention_type

"ITN" (acts in bed) or "IRS" (acts on indoor resting mosquitoes, or indoor biting ones with get_OM_ento_snippet(irs_exposure = "indoor_biting")).

name

Name of the intervention, used for component ids and placeholders. Default: for a named list, intervention_type; for one intervention, the name of an om_vector_control() specification, else the description of a build_intervention() object unless "custom", else intervention_type. In placeholders, <name> is the name with each run of characters other than letters and digits replaced by _ (e.g. "Interceptor G2" gives "@Interceptor_G2_deterrency@").

decay

"fixed" (default: decays written from the interventions) or "placeholder" (decay parameters as placeholders, e.g. when the attrition varies between scenarios).

Value

The updated baseList.

See also

deploy_OM_vector_control, om_scenario_values, get_ITN_params

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Built-in and custom dummy-host nets (other nets: list_ITN_params())
ig2 = om_vector_control(get_ITN_params("Interceptor G2", "Kibondo",
                                       mode = "dummy_host"),
                        halflife_attrition = 2 * 365, shape_attrition = 2)
custom = om_vector_control(
    c(Deterrency = 0.3, KillingDuringHostSeekingAbsolute = 0.5,
      PostPrandial = 0.4),
    halflife_attrition = 2 * 365, shape_attrition = 2)
nets = list(IG2 = ig2, custom = custom)
om_ento  = get_OM_ento_snippet("Anopheles gambiae ss/coluzzii",
                               activity = def_activity_patterns())
baseList$OMVersion = 49L     # dummy hosts need schema >= 46
baseList = define_OM_entomology(baseList, om_ento, seasonality = rep(1, 12))
baseList = define_OM_vector_control(baseList, nets, name = "ITN",
                                    decay = "placeholder")
schedule = om_campaigns("2021-01-01", "2027-01-01", every = "3 years",
                        coverage = "@cov@", by_year = TRUE,
                        end_date = "2030-01-01")
baseList = deploy_OM_vector_control(baseList, "ITN", schedule)
# The user's scenario table, filled with the values of the placeholders
scens = expand.grid(net = c("IG2", "custom"), attrition = c(2, 3),
                    cov2021 = c(0.5, 0.8), cov2024 = 0.6, cov2027 = 0.6)
scens = om_scenario_values(scens, baseList, "ITN", net = "net",
                           halflife = "attrition")
} # }
